newsitem.title: UK: Down trend continues on UK grain futures.
newsitem.headline: Down trend continues on UK grain futures.

text.p: UK grain futures remained under pressure in active trading on Monday.
"Nothing has changed since Friday," said a trader.
Prices continued to fall owing to strong currency combining with a higher north European crop than originally forecast and a bearish USDA crop report on Friday.
Traders said farmers were also selling.
"Farmers have seen the market falling quite fast and have decided now is the time to sell," said a trader.
Not everyone agreed that there was farm selling.

"It depends who you talk to as to whether farmers are selling or not, but to some extent that reflect's how successful that person has been in getting the farmers to sell to him," said another trader.
Despite a rally towards the close, wheat futures closed 1.35 to 0.85 stg down after trading 923 lots.
Barley futures came under increased selling pressure during the afternoon with closing values 2.50 to two stg down against one stg lower at the end of the moring session.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were unchanged and tradeless.
On the UK fob market feed wheat for February fetched 105 stg a tonne ex-east coast ports.
Delivered market trade was "reasonable" with milling wheat 11 percent protein fetching 125 stg a tonne for Nov in Liverpool while 126 and 125.50 stg was paid for Jan/Mar.
Feed wheat for Oct was trading at around 102 to 103 stg in East Anglia with New Year delivery material fetching 106 and 105.50 stg in the same area.
Feed barley was making 105.50 stg for Nov in the east of England and 105.50 and 106 stg in the west.
